identity_note: This deposit and the 'Genome Biology 2026, HeLa ISG15-KO' row of the handoff §6 candidate table are the SAME candidate. Confirmed from the article's Availability of data and materials plus reference 88, which cites the accession under the deposited title verbatim. The two §6 rows collapse to one.

Guo 2010 ribosome profiling — cited, not generated by this study

requirements.artefact: Additional file 2, sheet 'Table S1' — one workbook, six sheets named Table S1 through Table S6

shape.identifier_column: Uniprot ID and Gene name, both populated on every row
shape.selection_representation: Cluster membership. Sites not retained at p < 0.01 are absent from the table rather than flagged in it, so the table is the selected set, not the tested set.

requirements.note: Comparable in kind to the anchor's SUPP_DATA_1: one row per site, an identifier, a position. Cleaner than the anchor in two respects that matter on this project — no multi-protein razor cells and no isoform accessions, both of which are load-bearing problems on PXD018299 (82% multi-protein mapping, 30% isoform razor picks). Whether that reflects FragPipe's site table or the authors' trimming is not determined here.

criterion_recorded.search: FragPipe v21.1, LFQ-ubiquitin workflow, default settings including 1% FDR; SwissProt January 2024 release, 20,644 human sequences; precursor tolerance 10 ppm, fragment 20 ppm; stricttrypsin, up to three missed cleavages; carbamidomethyl fixed, Met oxidation / protein N-term acetyl / GG-K variable; yields the combined_site_K_114.0429 table
criterion_recorded.downstream: Perseus v.1.6.2.1; MaxLFQ intensities log2-transformed; normalised by per-sample median subtraction; sites with fewer than three valid values in at least one replicate group discarded; missing values imputed from a normal distribution around the detection limit; two-way ANOVA on treatment (Mock/IFN/ISG15) x genotype (WT / ISG15-/-), giving three p-values per site
criterion_recorded.selection_threshold: p < 0.01 on at least one of the three p-values
criterion_recorded.multiplicity_correction: none stated for the GG-peptidomics arm

requirements.note: The stated criterion is the one that selects the published claim set, so R2 passes on the proposed v2 wording as well as on v1.

requirements.artefact: Design.xlsx, single sheet, 44 rows, two blocks headed GlyGly and Shotgun
requirements.completeness: All six groups carry exactly three replicates in both arms, 18 distinct condition labels per arm, no gap and no duplicate. The GlyGly and shotgun arms carry identical condition sequences position by position, which corroborates the methods' statement that the shotgun samples are 1% aliquots of the same preparations — an independent check, not a restatement.
requirements.acquisition_order: Randomised with respect to condition; WT_mock occupies runs 1, 11 and 17.
requirements.limit_of_this_pass: Design.xlsx maps RUN to condition. The requirement is a column-to-condition mapping and is satisfied in the 'any grain' sense, but the last hop — from a quantitative column in the FragPipe site table to a run — is not in this file. It lives in the archive, so the mapping chain is complete only if the processed table's column names carry the run identifiers. Unverified.
requirements.sole_carrier: Design.xlsx. An sdrf.tsv and an experiment_annotation.tsv exist inside Search_GlyGly.zip, but both were opened and neither carries a biological condition — see archive_analysis.three_condition_mappings_now_exist. R3 passes on one non-standard spreadsheet and nothing else.

instances_today: A file-count argument was advanced against this deposit's identity from a number with no derivation.
Source 8 was recorded as exhausted with the SDRF positively absent, from a listing containing two unopened archives.
R3 was recorded as resting on three carriers including a community standard, on the strength of two filenames.
recurring_error_shape.shape: Content asserted from a name or a count, without opening the thing. Three instances in one session, each caught only by opening the artefact afterwards.
recurring_error_shape.the_project's_own_words_for_it: Read the artefact, not the prose about it. The principle was already in learnings; what was missing was a rule that makes following it checkable rather than a matter of remembering.
recurring_error_shape.structural_fix: The container rung proposed under source 8. With it, none of the three would have been recordable: each was a determination at a grain the ladder would have refused.

recurring_error_shape.note: No file readable by an existing adapter is present. The claim-bearing table is combined_site_K_114.0429.tsv (7.1 MB), exactly the table the methods name, sitting at the top level of Search_GlyGly.zip. It is FragPipe format; the platform reads MaxQuant today. R4 therefore fails on adapter availability alone, not on any property of the deposit.
recurring_error_shape.exhaustion_argument: Eighteen per-run subfolders and the shotgun archive were not opened. The FAIL stands anyway because FragPipe per-run output is pepXML and psm.tsv, which no existing adapter reads either, so no unopened item in this archive is of a type that could flip the verdict. This is a short-circuit of the deepest-grain rule grounded in a claim about FragPipe's output format, and it is stated here so a checker can reject it rather than having to reconstruct it.

recurring_error_shape.consequence_for_the_adapter_decision: The build target is identified and bounded: one TSV in a documented format, with the search fully parameterised alongside it. The re-search alternative is dead. What remains open is the I15 question, which is about ingestion policy rather than about this file.

SUPERSEDES.prior_determination: Recorded earlier the same day as 'exhausted: true — positively absent from the retrieved listing. This is a determination, not a gap.'
SUPERSEDES.status: WRONG, and wrong by rule rather than by luck.
SUPERSEDES.analysis: The absence was determined against a listing that contained two unopened archives. WALK-STANDARD §2 requires the deepest applicable grain on every listed item before a FAIL or a positive absence; §4 source 7 says a listing that stops at a container is not exhausted; and the container-grain gap had been named explicitly in the same session. The determination was made anyway. This is the PXD074990 defect reproduced inside the walk that exists to prevent it — an absence asserted from a shallow grain, at a point where the shallowness was known.
SUPERSEDES.correction_to_the_standard: The §3 grain ladder needs an explicit container rung between G1 and G2: an archive or folder listed but not expanded is G1, and no absence may be determined from it. Without that rung, 'exhausted' at G1 reads as legitimate.

counts.note_on_exhausted_count: Down from 6: source 8 was wrongly counted as exhausted and is now correctly not. A count that only rises is not being checked.

archive_analysis.contents: 18 per-run subfolders named to match the raw files, plus 24 files
archive_analysis.b2684_absence_holds: The subfolders run B2652 to B2688 in steps of two with B2684 absent, identical to the top-level raw listing. The absence is confirmed at a second, deeper grain and is not a PRIDE upload artefact.
archive_analysis.join_hazard_holds: The sample-15 subfolder is B2680_..._FRIMP_Lissa_GlyGly_15_Rerun while all others are ..._FRIMP_GlyGly_Lissa_N. The token transposition is systematic through the processing chain, not introduced at deposition. An index-based join is required at every stage, not just at the raw-file stage.

three_condition_mappings_now_exist.status: RETRACTED the same day it was written. Both archive files were opened and NEITHER carries a biological condition. Design.xlsx is the sole carrier after all — the original note, which this block had superseded, was right.

sdrf_tsv.shape: 18 data rows, 12 columns, all of them comment[...]
sdrf_tsv.populated_columns: comment[data file], plus five search-parameter columns whose values are constant across all 18 runs
sdrf_tsv.verdict: This is a search-parameter SDRF. It describes how the data were searched and says nothing about what any sample is. No genotype, no treatment, no replicate structure.

experiment_annotation_tsv.shape: 18 data rows; columns file, sample, sample_name, condition, replicate
experiment_annotation_tsv.condition_column: holds the instrument batch number (B2652, B2654, ...), 18 distinct values — one per run
experiment_annotation_tsv.verdict: FragPipe was configured with each run as its own condition and no replication. Biological grouping was deferred entirely to Perseus, so no grouped quantification happened at the FragPipe stage.

three_condition_mappings_now_exist.run_sets_agree: Both files cover the same 18 runs; the sets are identical. There is no disagreement to find, because there is nothing to disagree about.
three_condition_mappings_now_exist.the_actual_finding: The deposit's machine-readable design metadata contains no design. A consumer taking the standard route — the SDRF — recovers search parameters and learns nothing about genotype or treatment. The experimental design exists only in a free-text Condition column of a non-standard spreadsheet at the top level, outside the archive. Every published claim in this deposit depends on that mapping, and it is carried by the least durable artefact present. This is a claim about deposit practice, measured rather than asserted, and it belongs in the thesis.

tolerance_discrepancy.status: RESOLVED against fragger.params. The paper is correct on both numbers; sdrf.tsv is wrong on both.

fragger_params_says.precursor_true_tolerance: 20 ppm — a different parameter, used for calibration and scoring

adjudication.paper_precursor_10ppm: CORRECT — it is the search window.
adjudication.sdrf_precursor_20ppm: WRONG as a report of the search window. It has taken precursor_true_tolerance, a different parameter, and labelled it the precursor mass tolerance.
adjudication.sdrf_fragment_25ppm: WRONG and unexplained. 25 ppm appears nowhere in fragger.params.

tolerance_discrepancy.correction_to_my_framing: The conflict was raised as 'paper says 10, deposit says 20', with fragger.params to adjudicate. That framing treated the deposit as a single voice and implicitly weighted it against the publication. The deposit is not one voice: its parameter file and its SDRF disagree with each other, and the publication agrees with the parameter file. The benign reading offered at the time — exporter defaults — is right in direction and wrong in detail, since 20 tracks a real parameter and 25 tracks none.
tolerance_discrepancy.compounded_finding: sdrf.tsv now carries no experimental design AND misreports two search parameters. The one community-standard machine-readable artefact in this deposit is the least reliable thing in it. That is a sharper claim about deposit practice than the design finding alone, and it is the same claim: the standard route to this deposit's metadata is the route that fails.
tolerance_discrepancy.for_the_taxonomy: This instance is not D5. D5 is a parameter stated without an implementation. Here the parameter is stated, an implementation is deposited, and a third artefact contradicts both. Whether that is a class or an instance of an existing one is a HYPOTHESIS.md question and out of this walk's scope.

examples: GG capped at 2 occurrences per peptide (variable_mod_10 = 114.04293 K 2)
parameters_the_deposit_resolves_that_the.database: 2024-06-12-decoys-contam-UP000005640_9606.fasta.fas, under a 01_2024 folder. Human reference proteome with decoys and contaminants. The parent directory is named for four species; the file used is human-only. Whether it matches the paper's '20,644 human sequences' is not determinable from the path.
parameters_the_deposit_resolves_that_the.why_it_matters: The search step is not merely reproducible from the deposit — the deposit is strictly more informative than the methods section for this stage. It strengthens the isolation argument: underdetermination in this candidate is confined to the Perseus imputation, and nowhere else in the chain.
parameters_the_deposit_resolves_that_the.qualification: calibrate_mass = 2 means MSFragger optimised tolerances per run, so no single stated tolerance is the operative one end to end. The correct stated number is still not the number used.

d5_position_after_the_archive.what_is_now_pinned: The search step is fully parameterised in the deposit: fragger.params, fragpipe.workflow, msbooster_params.txt, the IonQuant and ProteinProphet file lists, the FragPipe manifest and the run log. Search is reproducible from deposited artefacts rather than from prose. The site table itself reconciles exactly to the paper's stated 15,619 GG-modified sites.
d5_position_after_the_archive.what_remains_free: The Perseus boundary — and it is two steps, not one.
d5_position_after_the_archive.step_1_zero_handling: combined_site_K_114.0429.tsv encodes missing values as 0.0 and never as blank; 28.2% of intensity cells are zero. Perseus expects blank or NaN. A zero-to-missing conversion must have occurred and the methods do not state it. It sits upstream of both the valid-value filter and the imputation, so a reconstruction must choose it before it can reach the imputation at all.
d5_position_after_the_archive.step_2_imputation: Width, downshift and seed unstated in the paper and absent from the deposit.
d5_position_after_the_archive.correction: An earlier entry in this file recorded the underdetermination as isolated to a single step. That was written before the site table was opened and is WRONG. Two unstated steps, and the divergence of any reconstruction is attributable to their combination unless the zero-handling is pinned separately.
d5_position_after_the_archive.consequence_that_survives: Everything upstream of the Perseus boundary is pinned by deposited parameter files, and the published claim set joins to the search output on an exact key with no losses. The instrument is still cleaner than the anchor's; it has two free parameters rather than one, not an unbounded number.
d5_position_after_the_archive.caveat: Isolation is an argument from what is present, and it holds only if the FragPipe parameters actually reproduce the 15,619 sites. The row count matches the paper's figure, which is consistent with but not proof of reproducibility — the paper's number and the deposited table have the same origin.

site_table.shape: 15,619 data rows, one row per site, 60 columns: 5 identity, Best Localization Probability, then per-run blocks of 18 for Localization Probability, Intensity and MaxLFQ Intensity
site_table.key: Index, formatted ACC_Knnn — identical in form to Table S1's Lysine position column
site_table.join_to_published_claims: All 3,344 Table S1 keys are present in the site table; none absent. Exact join, no reconciliation step.
site_table.implication_for_the_schema: REQUIRED_COLUMNS needs no FragPipe spelling of Reverse or Potential contaminant — the concept does not apply, because filtering happened upstream of the artefact. The anchor's decoy/contaminant loss category is structurally zero here, as registered in advance.
site_table.open_question_now_closed_and_a_new_one_o: The cleanliness is FragPipe's, not the authors' trimming. Whether that means the anchor's multi-protein and isoform rates are MaxQuant-razor artefacts, or means FragPipe is making the same assignment without exposing it, is not distinguishable from this table. combined_modified_peptide.tsv and combined_ion.tsv would distinguish them.
site_table.provisional_figure_do_not_inherit: Applying 'at least three non-zero values in at least one replicate group' to the Intensity columns leaves 12,220 sites against 3,344 published. Provisional and probably on the wrong columns — the methods imply MaxLFQ. Recorded with its defect; re-derive before use.

design_join_hazard.what: Design.xlsx keys runs by a stem (e.g. CMB-1265_FRIMP_GlyGly_Lissa-7) that is a substring of the deposited filename (B2664_Ap_IonOpt_CMB-1265_FRIMP_GlyGly_Lissa-7.raw) for 17 of 18 GlyGly runs. For one run it is not.
design_join_hazard.the_exception: Design says CMB-1265_FRIMP_GlyGly_Lissa-15_Rerun. The deposited file is B2680_Ap_IonOpt_CMB-1265_FRIMP_Lissa-GlyGly-15_rerun.raw — the GlyGly and Lissa tokens are transposed, the separator changes from underscore to hyphen, and the case of 'rerun' differs. A literal join yields zero hits.
design_join_hazard.why_it_matters: That run is WT_IFN_rep3. A join that drops it silently loses one third of the WT_IFN arm — and the WT_IFN arm is the exact arm the anchor's R1 result turned on, where none of the fourteen published targets has a measured WT_IFN value and log2FC is set by downshift_sd instead. The same arm is the fragile one in both deposits, for unrelated reasons.
design_join_hazard.adapter_consequence: Join runs by extracted sample index, never by literal filename stem. An index-based join maps all 18. This is a named requirement on any FragPipe adapter, not a detail.
design_join_hazard.test_artefact_disclosed: A naive substring test also flagged Lissa-1 and CMB-1263_1 as ambiguous. That is prefix collision in the test (Lissa-1 matches Lissa-18), not a defect in the data. Recorded so the count of three mismatches is not mistaken for three findings — there is one.

finding_1.what: Sample 15 is deposited only as a rerun. B2680 is exactly the in-sequence slot for sample 15 under B = 2652 + 2(n-1), so the rerun was acquired in sequence and the superseded original acquisition is not in this deposit and not in this number series.

finding_2.what: The B-series is exactly in step for samples 1 through 16 and offset by one slot from 17 onward: Lissa-17 is B2686 where the series predicts B2684, and Lissa-18 is B2688 where it predicts B2686. One un-deposited acquisition occupies B2684, between samples 16 and 17.

acquisition_absences.correction_to_prior_reading: An earlier turn suggested B2684 might be the superseded original of sample 15. The arithmetic rules that out: B2684 sits between samples 16 and 17, and sample 15's slot is occupied by the rerun itself. These are two independent absences, not one.
acquisition_absences.class: selection at acquisition grain, D1-shaped. Two instances, both recorded, neither counted — the deposit gives no way to determine what either absent acquisition was.

cross_reference: WT_ISG15_rep3 is Lissa-13 / B2676, which is the 510 size outlier recorded under listing_analysis. So the two anomalous GlyGly runs fall in different groups — WT_IFN_rep3 carries the join hazard, WT_ISG15_rep3 carries the size outlier. Neither is in a mock group.

listing_analysis.completeness: GlyGly runs are indexed Lissa-1 through Lissa-18 with no gap; shotgun runs are indexed _1 through _18 with no gap. 18 GlyGly runs is exactly two genotypes x three treatments x three replicates, one run per sample, confirming from the listing that no fractionation was performed — the methods said as much and the listing now corroborates it independently.
listing_analysis.two_acquisition_batches: GlyGly on Ap_IonOpt / CMB-1265; shotgun on 2p_Ionopticks10_trapPM7 / CMB-1263. Different instrument-setup strings and a threefold to fivefold size difference. Recorded; no inference drawn.

m2_reconciliation.method: openpyxl read of Additional file 2; cluster counts tallied from the Cluster column of Table S1; published counts taken from the article Results and compared afterwards, not during.
m2_reconciliation.agreement_with_published: Exact on every stated figure. Cluster 1a 20; cluster 1 total 671; clusters 2-5 total 2,672; and 456 distinct Uniprot IDs across cluster 1, which is the published substrate count reproduced independently from the table rather than taken from the prose.

discrepancy.what: Table S1 holds 3,344 data rows, of which 3,343 carry a cluster label. Excel row 1998, index 1996, Q9C0E8 / LNPK / Q9C0E8_K324, has an empty Cluster cell.
discrepancy.where: It sits on the cluster 3 / cluster 4 boundary, between O75396_K178 (cluster 3) and Q9Y490_K869 (cluster 4).
discrepancy.consequence: The published counts sum to 3,343 and therefore exclude it. Clusters 3 and 4 are both ubiquitin clusters, so whichever it belongs to it is a ubiquitin site: the ISG15 claim set of 671 is unaffected. The published ubiquitin total is short by one against the deposited table.
discrepancy.class: A site present in the published claim table and in no published count, whose cluster — and therefore whose modifier attribution — is unresolvable from the artefact. D3-shaped, not D5. Recorded as an instance; not counted, and not a defeat of anything in this walk.
discrepancy.alternative_reading_not_excluded: A formatting gap at a sort boundary rather than a substantive omission. Nothing in the artefact distinguishes the two.

observations_bearing_on_D5.observation: Imputation parameters are not stated. The methods say missing values were imputed from a normal distribution around the detection limit, and give no width, no downshift and no seed.
observations_bearing_on_D5.why_it_matters: This is underdetermination by omission, and it is the same defect that blocks PXD055843 at I15. Imputation is load-bearing on this project's own evidence. The test itself is fully specified, so if a reconstruction diverges here the divergence is attributable to the imputation alone — a cleaner D5 instance than the anchor, where the test's implementation is also missing.

observations_bearing_on_D5.observation: The selection threshold is an uncorrected p < 0.01 taken as the minimum over three ANOVA p-values, applied across 15,619 GG-modified sites discovered at search level.
observations_bearing_on_D5.why_it_matters: Stated, not omitted — so it is not underdetermination. A reconstruction choosing a corrected test would withdraw support from a fraction of the claims by disagreeing with a stated choice rather than by filling a gap. Whether that counts as D5 or as a distinct class is a question for HYPOTHESIS.md and is out of this walk's scope.

observations_bearing_on_D5.observation: The same methods section applies a permutation FDR of 0.05 with S0 = 1 to the shotgun arm while applying no correction to the GG-peptidomics arm.
observations_bearing_on_D5.why_it_matters: Two criteria of different stringency inside one paper. Recorded as a fact about the publication; no inference drawn.

observations_bearing_on_D5.observation: Cluster membership assigns modifier identity (cluster 1 = ISG15, clusters 2-5 = ubiquitin), downstream of the p < 0.01 selection.
observations_bearing_on_D5.why_it_matters: Attribution, not selection — D3 territory, not D1 and not D5. Relevant because the anchor does not separate these two stages and this candidate does.

corrections_to_prior_reasoning.what: A file-count argument was advanced against the identification of this deposit: eighteen GG samples plus eighteen shotgun aliquots imply roughly thirty-six MS runs, which was treated as straining against a 607-file deposit.
corrections_to_prior_reasoning.outcome: WRONG. The identification is confirmed. The deposit evidently carries more per run than raw files.
corrections_to_prior_reasoning.class: An inference at G0 was allowed to lean against a hypothesis it had no standing to test. Same shape as the PXD074990 defect, one level down. It produced no verdict, so nothing had to be reversed.

corrections_to_prior_reasoning.what: STEP2-R1-SCAN.md recorded R1 for this candidate as 'PASS-provisional at G1'.
corrections_to_prior_reasoning.outcome: Not a verdict in the WALK-STANDARD §2 vocabulary. The correct verdict at that evidence is UNRESOLVED, as recorded above.
corrections_to_prior_reasoning.class: Vocabulary drift in the first application of the standard.

verdict_reason: R1 and R2 both PASS at publication grade. R3 and R4 remain UNRESOLVED pending the deposit itself — sources 6 through 9 not reached. This candidate now has everything the D5 replication needs from the publication side: a keyable site-grain claim set, a stated selecting criterion, and an unstated imputation step for the reconstruction to diverge on. What it does not yet have is a demonstrated route from the deposit to a reconstruction, which is the FragPipe-adapter question.
